findings.claim: The new `ContainsKey` guards silently discard a member whose key duplicates an earlier member's key. Repro: a `[MessagePackObject]` with `[Key(0)] int FirstMember` and `[Key(0)] int SecondMember`, or two members with the same string key. Base threw from `Dictionary.Add`, a loud generator or analyzer failure; `DynamicObjectResolver` also rejects duplicate keys at runtime. Head reports no diagnostic, and the generated formatter serializes only FirstMember, so SecondMember's data is lost on every round trip. This also changes behaviour when `SuppressSourceGeneration` is unset, which the acceptance criteria forbid.

On head no MsgPack/AD0001/generator diagnostic is produced and the generated source never mentions SecondMember, so both tests fail.

findings.claim: The same silent drop applies in the second member loop (the hunks at new lines 1163 and 1179). A duplicate int or string key there is also discarded without a diagnostic, so the defect is not confined to the first loop.

findings.claim: The new `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys skips every later per-member check for that member. One example is the `[MessagePackFormatter]` attribute validation that follows (MessageFormatterMustBeMessagePackFormatter). A member that both mixes key kinds and has an invalid formatter now gets only the mix diagnostic. The formatter diagnostic is dropped, though it is still reported when the key kind is fixed.
